scenario_prompt: Write the response to this scored RFP question, worth 25% of the RFP's overall technical score: "Describe the migration approach and cutover plan." Context: the migration moves load-matching and carrier-settlement systems off on-premises Microsoft SQL Server (28 instances, 620 Hyper-V virtual machines) onto Google Cloud (Google Compute Engine for compute, Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL for the data layer), within a 2-year, $4,200,000 programme, with proposals due 2026-11-15 and the buyer's next compliance audit opening in 6 months. Return only the answer text, no section headers beyond what the answer itself needs.
text:
What counts as customer source material here: the RFP question text and the context you gave me (28 SQL Server instances, 620 Hyper-V VMs, GCE + Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL, 2-year/$4.2M programme, proposals due 2026-11-15, next compliance audit opening in 6 months). I'll treat that as the only supplied customer material — nothing else. No other source material was supplied, so PF-3.3 cannot fire beyond these facts, and every other term is judged by the deletion test alone.

**An RFP answer**

Today load-matching and carrier-settlement run on 28 on-premises SQL Server instances spread across 620 Hyper-V virtual machines — an estate your compliance audit must cover again in 6 months, before this migration can plausibly be complete under any but the most compressed timeline. [PF-1.2 GAP: no stated cost of running this estate today — dollar run-rate, incident count, or capacity constraint was not supplied] We propose moving this estate to Google Compute Engine for compute and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL for the data layer, over a 24-month, $4,200,000 programme, cutting over before your audit boundary where the plan allows and treating the remaining scope as a defined post-audit phase rather than a forced compression.

**Migration approach**

You need a phased, application-boundary-led migration: load-matching and carrier-settlement move as separate workstreams, each re-platformed from SQL Server to Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL and re-hosted from Hyper-V VMs to Compute Engine, so a failure in one workstream never blocks or rolls back the other. [PF-1.9] Sequencing is discovery-first: every one of the 28 SQL Server instances is inventoried for schema, stored-procedure logic, and cross-instance dependency before any wave is assigned a cutover date, because T-SQL-to-PostgreSQL conversion risk — not raw VM count — is what should set the pace. [PF-2.14 REVIEW (commitment): wave sequencing and count depend on discovery findings not yet in hand; treat any wave schedule in the SOW as provisional until discovery closes]

Within each wave, data migration runs continuous replication from the source SQL Server instance into Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL, validated row-by-row against the source before that wave is scheduled to cut over. [PF-1.17 GAP: no named validation tooling or reconciliation method supplied — a specific replication/CDC product and row-comparison method needs to be named before this becomes a checkable proof point] Compute for each workstream is rebuilt natively on Compute Engine rather than lifted-and-shifted as Hyper-V images, since load-matching and carrier-settlement logic tied to SQL Server-specific behavior needs re-validation against PostgreSQL semantics regardless of how the VM layer moves. [PF-2.14 REVIEW (commitment): "rebuilt natively" implies a specific re-platforming commitment per workstream; confirm this holds for all 28 instances or scope the exceptions before the proposal ships]

**Cutover plan**

Before: settlement and load-matching transactions write to on-premises SQL Server today. After: the same transactions write to Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL on Google Cloud, with the source instance decommissioned only after a defined parallel-run period confirms output parity. [PF-1.5] Each wave's cutover follows the same four steps: freeze writes to the source instance, complete final delta replication, run reconciliation checks against source, then redirect application traffic to the Compute Engine/Cloud SQL target — with rollback to the SQL Server source available until reconciliation passes. [PF-2.14 REVIEW (commitment): the write-freeze window and rollback threshold are commitments to specific downtime and reversibility; confirm the acceptable freeze duration with the buyer before this is stated as a fixed procedure]

Your next compliance audit opens in 6 months, inside a 24-month programme — so the cutover plan sequences the earliest waves to land before that audit window opens, and explicitly carries any workstream that cannot complete discovery, migration, and a validated parallel run in time into a post-audit wave rather than compressing validation to hit the date. [PF-1.25 GAP: no named audit owner or role supplied — the person accountable for audit readiness was not identified, so this outcome cannot yet be addressed to them by name] [PF-2.17 REVIEW (compliance): which compliance framework governs this audit, and whether Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL and Compute Engine already meet its specific controls, was not supplied and is not asserted here]

**Metrics and baseline**

Migration scope is 28 SQL Server instances and 620 Hyper-V VMs, both stated by the buyer. [PF-1.13, PF-1.14 — source: buyer-supplied RFP context] [PF-2.11 GAP: no current downtime, transaction-volume, or performance baseline for load-matching or carrier-settlement was supplied; these would need to be captured during discovery before a target SLA or performance-parity metric can be set]

## Unresolved before this document is sent

| Marker | Rule | What is needed |
|---|---|---|
| No stated cost of the current estate | PF-1.2 | Dollar run-rate, incident frequency, or capacity constraint tied to the current SQL Server/Hyper-V footprint |
| Wave sequencing depends on discovery not yet done | PF-2.14 (commitment) | Confirmation that the SOW's wave schedule is marked provisional pending discovery |
| No named validation/reconciliation tooling | PF-1.17 | A specific replication or CDC product and row-comparison method |
| "Rebuilt natively" claimed for all 28 instances | PF-2.14 (commitment) | Confirmation this holds across all instances, or named exceptions |
| Freeze window and rollback threshold unspecified | PF-2.14 (commitment) | Agreed acceptable downtime window and rollback pass/fail criteria |
| No named audit owner | PF-1.25 | The role or person accountable for audit readiness |
| Compliance framework and current control status unstated | PF-2.17 (compliance) | Which framework governs the audit, and confirmation Cloud SQL/Compute Engine meet its specific controls today |
| No current performance/downtime baseline | PF-2.11 | Baseline transaction volume, downtime tolerance, or performance figures for load-matching and carrier-settlement |
